Optimal.Notes: High shader and texture detail look great at native 1280x800 with no upscaling needed; a 7 W TDP cap is comfortably sufficient and keeps the fan quiet. This is the recommended everyday profile.

profiles.Summary: Portal 2 is a Source Engine game from 2011 with very modest PC requirements, running natively on the Steam Deck as a Verified title and easily hitting 60 fps at full resolution with low TDP. The game is lightweight enough that even the battery-saving profile delivers a smooth, stable experience with plenty of playtime.
profiles.BasisNote: No dedicated Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from the 2011 Source Engine minimum requirements and the Deck's RDNA 2 GPU, which vastly exceeds them. On your first run, confirm the frame counter stays at 60 in the largest test chambers and lower the TDP cap further if battery life is the priority.

MaxBattery.Notes: A 4 W TDP and locked 40 Hz refresh is more than enough for this Source Engine title; the GPU clock is capped low to minimise draw. Drop shader and shadow detail to Low for maximum efficiency.

MaxPerformance.Notes: Portal 2 is so light that Very High / 8× MSAA still sits comfortably at 60 fps with no TDP limit; the chip will self-govern well below 15 W. No FSR or upscaling is needed at any setting level.

Optimal.Notes: Native 1280x800 at high settings holds a rock-solid 60 fps with comfortable battery life; this is the sweet spot for Portal 2 on the Deck OLED.

profiles.Summary: Portal 2 is a native Linux-compatible Source engine title that runs excellently on the Steam Deck, achieving high frame rates even at modest TDP settings. As a Valve-developed game with full controller support and Verified status, it is one of the smoothest experiences available on the device.
profiles.BasisNote: No specific Deck player reports were available; profiles are estimated from Portal 2's very light Source engine requirements (well below Deck GPU capability) and Valve's Verified rating. On first run, confirm the frame rate holds at your chosen cap in the most visually busy test chambers, and adjust TDP down if battery drain is higher than expected.

MaxBattery.Notes: Renders at 960x600 with FSR upscaling to keep TDP extremely low; the Source engine is very light and this profile squeezes maximum playtime without sacrificing smooth 40 fps pacing.

MaxPerformance.Notes: The Source engine easily saturates the Deck at 90 Hz with max settings; battery drain is significant but Portal 2 is short enough that this is viable for a focused play session.
